title: Out-think the field
question: Thirty-six simulated rivals and a blind panel say Caplet's plan is the field's default answer. What can Caplet XR say that no other team can, and which of tonight's ideas earn a place in the IPS?
serves: North stars 3 and 4; Wharton's Investment Strategy, Portfolio Analysis and Creativity criteria; the IPS rewrite (near-final Sat 31 Oct)
essence: The ladder-first structure is what every AI-assisted rival writes; Caplet's edge is the reason (her income can shrink in the same slump), where it breaks, and the two-cost range.

Jun's audit killed two of our own claims: the rising stock share is a bonds-being-spent effect, not a hook, and certainty costs nothing at the median once rivals are matched on misses; its real price is the best years.
decided: 6-0: answer Book 7's composition question with XR's mechanism (one holding redeems, one cheque goes out, nobody trades); the rising share is one clause at most
6-0: name both breaks (the build and the 2033 coupon gap) by cause and a real year, never a probability; drop 'small'
5-0-1: human capital stays 'her income can shrink', never 'moves with stocks'
3-0-3: the 2033 set-aside must use a permitted holding; direct T-bills are out
seeds: Who absorbs a bad year: Laura's half, then the top, never the bottom (Amara) vs L-10's $10k hold-back
Tail dependence and the 2028 income link (Kai)
changes: Thinking only, no draft change. Recommendations sent to the rewrite thread: keel/ips_rewrite/inbox/2026-10-28_rivals-and-panel.md
